previous_disclosures.summary: Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2023 grew 60% to $903 million compared to fiscal year 2022, and the company started production of the NVIDIA DRIVE Orin autonomous vehicle SOC and introduced next-generation NVIDIA DRIVE Thor.

current_disclosures.summary: Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2024 increased 21%, primarily reflecting growth in self-driving platforms.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $1.1 billion, up 21% from fiscal year 2023. The company partnered with MediaTek for automotive SoCs, collaborated with Foxconn on electric vehicles, and expanded NVIDIA DRIVE platform adoption with multiple OEMs.

materiality_analysis.reason: Automotive revenue growth slowed significantly from 60% to 21%, and the disclosure introduces specific new partnerships (MediaTek, Foxconn) and expanded OEM adoption (BYD, XPENG, etc.), indicating a material change in growth trajectory and strategic alliances.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Deceleration of automotive revenue growth and new strategic partnerships

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures report specific segment revenue performance and its primary drivers for fiscal year 2024. NVDA reports Automotive segment revenue growth of 21% driven by self-driving platforms, while AMD reports Data Center segment revenue growth of 94% driven by Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Both illustrate strong sequential revenue expansion in key strategic segments, though the magnitude and specific product drivers differ.

sentences.text: Automotive revenue for the fiscal year 2024 was up 21%.
The increase primarily reflected growth in self-driving platforms.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
